title: Arbitrary bases and cardinal dimension

based_on.title: Pregeometries and minimal types
based_on.pages: §1 Proposition1.7, Definition1.8 and Remark1.9, pp.2–3 (revision2008-11-11); infinite basis comparison expanded

summary: Extend independent sets to arbitrary bases, compare infinite basis cardinalities, and define dimension over a parameter set.
abstract: Finite generators have independent bases of a well-defined finite size. What happens when a closed set needs infinitely many generators? Finite character keeps the union of a chain independent, allowing a maximal independent extension. Two such bases need not match point by point, but finite supports cover one basis using the other and force their cardinalities to agree. Their common cardinal is dimension. Treating a parameter set as already available gives another pregeometry and defines relative dimension without subtracting infinite cardinals. These constructions apply to the algebraic closure already obtained in strongly minimal structures; identity closure makes the distinction between absolute and relative dimension explicit.
